note: Swappable grammar pack (R46, §9.3/§9.11) for the object-storage line. Machine-checked wall between namespaces: 'decision' strings appear while the player decides or loses (labels, terms, refusals, alerts, status rungs) and stay SOBER per §9.3 clauses 2-3; 'flavour' carries the recognition comedy for quiet surfaces. Authenticity law for this line (§9.3/§9.11): the drama is ARITHMETIC's — the degraded read nobody scheduled, the comb draining one object at a time, the invoice with a viral file's name on it — and 'there is no dramatic attacker' (§1.3 verbatim); abuse exists only as complaint, discovery, vendor silence, and consequence. No payloads, commands, tool names-as-how-to, or technique instruction anywhere.

nodeId.desc: Board object the decision surface is about (storage node / bucket id).

availableAtTick.desc: Tick at which the queued intent or a freed hand presents.

slotName.desc: Socket designation on a node (PSU, uplink, drive bay).

bucketName.desc: A customer bucket by name — the unit the whole line is read in.

objectKey.desc: One object's key inside a bucket; the pebble, not the comb.

replicaCount.desc: Visible replica shadows behind an object (1, 2, 3, or stacked).

ninesDisplay.desc: The durability readout in nines form (§7.8 meter row).

verifiedPct.desc: Share of the comb verified inside the scrub cycle — the line's operational truth (§1.3).

scrubDaysLeft.desc: Days of scrub runway left before the failure-rate clock wins (§1.3).

rebuildPct.desc: Erasure-coding rebuild progress — the hole knitting shut (§1.3 visual).

failedDrives.desc: Simultaneous drive failures inside one rebuild window (§2.x EC math).

smallFileBillions.desc: A customer's tiny-file count in the millions — the routine catastrophe (§1.3).

egressTB.desc: Egress volume a spike moved this window (§1.3 economics).

invoiceAmount.desc: The disputed egress invoice figure (§6.6 bad-month row).

firmwareSerial.desc: Drive firmware batch identifier the defect marches down.

hour.desc: Clock hour a notice or ticket was filed at.

minute.desc: Clock minute a notice or ticket was filed at.

day.desc: Day of the quarter, for the intern's log.

decision.type.object-storage.name: Eleven Nines
decision.type.object-storage.codex: The durability line: cheap bytes, invisible until the day they are not. Replication versus erasure coding versus cost is arithmetic you can see; silent corruption and the scrub clock are arithmetic you can only schedule; and the routine catastrophe wears a customer's face — one upload of 400 million tiny files, one viral object on the wrong rate card. There is no dramatic attacker. The enemy is entropy and your own rebuild math.
decision.goal.object-storage.binding: Durability is arithmetic, not vibes: the scrub must complete faster than the failure rate, and the hands that audit placement are the same hands that answer the day customers finally notice.
decision.scarce.object-storage.qos: The degraded read outranks the healthy stripe, and the rebuild outranks both — at large enough scale you are always rebuilding something, so the queue that matters is the one verifying objects nobody has asked for yet.
decision.skin.object-storage.inspector: The Honeycomb in amber hex over comb-shadow — cells that tile outward as they grow, pebble objects falling into place with a soft triple-flash when replication lands, replica shadows fanned behind each stone or stacked three-deep when placement failed you, the meter read as how full and even the comb looks, and one gap-black hole somewhere you have not found yet.
decision.economy.object-storage.bad-month: An egress bill the customer disputes.
decision.relations.object-storage.mastery: The comb reads the quarter: scrubs finish before failures arrive, placement is audited while the shadows are still fanned, and the rate card was priced on the day the first viral file was still an ordinary one.
decision.relations.object-storage.distillate: Playbook: treat every nines figure as arithmetic you must show your work on — schedule verification like it is revenue, because it is the only proof you have; price exit as carefully as entry; and remember that a product nobody notices is not a product at rest, it is a product one bad day from being a headline.
decision.verbs.object-storage.transfer.1: Durability arithmetic transfers everywhere: any line where you promised more than one copy of something now asks you the same question — can I finish verifying everything before it changes?
decision.handover.object-storage.runs-out: Your rebuild bandwidth and your scrub clock. An empty comb is a bill you can pay down; a degraded stripe during a storm is a countdown you cannot.
decision.handover.object-storage.kills-you: Silent data loss: the corruption that copied itself into every replica, or the two simultaneous failures during a rebuild — the probability you could have computed and priced, and did not.
decision.handover.object-storage.customer-wants: The nines they were sold and never asked you to show. They never noticed you for months; the day they do, they will want the object.
decision.rosetta.object-storage.scrub: The scrub bandwidth share is the cgroup cage aimed at entropy instead of tenants: the same bet that background verification is work, and work competes for the same hands and the same drives.
decision.rosetta.object-storage.egress: The replication mix is the oversell ratio spent the other way: capacity you buy and bill to nobody, because the copies are priced in safety, not in seats.
decision.scenarios.object-storage.consistent-corr: A bug in the software layer corrupts consistently across all replicas (§1.3 verbatim): the redundancy you paid for agrees with the mistake, and the only thing that catches it is the verification you scheduled.
decision.scenarios.object-storage.metadata-apocal: A customer uploads everything they have in ten million small pieces and the metadata layer, not the data layer, is what dies (§1.3/§2.x): the routine catastrophe, arriving as a new signup.
decision.scenarios.object-storage.erasure-coding-: Two simultaneous disk failures during a rebuild — a probability you can actually compute and price (§2.x verbatim), which is the whole point of the durability dial.
decision.alert.degraded-read: {bucketName}: read came back degraded, {replicaCount} shadow(s) on file. Nothing is on fire. The comb is telling you where the fire will start.
decision.alert.scrub-behind: Scrub cycle at {verifiedPct} with {scrubDaysLeft} of runway. The card's operational truth, priced in hours: the scrub must complete faster than the failure rate (§1.3).
decision.alert.rebuild-storm: {failedDrives} failures inside one rebuild window; the hole is at {rebuildPct} knitted. Every storm that takes a second disk with it started as arithmetic nobody scheduled.
decision.alert.egress-spike: {objectKey} moved {egressTB} out this window. Depending on the pricing model you chose in shift 1, this line is either the best or the worst news in the inbox (§1.3).
decision.terms.durability-dial: Replication versus erasure coding at {ninesDisplay}: the dial IS the math (§2.x 'the point of the durability dial'); every notch trades rebuild bandwidth against the probability of the hole.
decision.terms.egress-rate-card: Storage at pennies, egress at a margin: 'egress billing is the main revenue line' (§1.3). The flat plan is a bet that nothing of yours gets interesting.
decision.terms.metadata-limits: Small-file pricing is metadata pricing: a million tiny objects is not a million pebbles, it is a million index writes — the routine catastrophe has a rate card if you author one (§1.3).
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.
decision.cac.object-storage.todo: §6.6 Companion B prices no object-storage acquisition channel; the §0.3 customer row ('developers, backup vendors') names WHO, not WHAT. Placeholder until the pricing pass — never invented.

flavour.ticket.subject.where-my-data: hi - quick question - where exactly is my data
flavour.ticket.body.where-my-data: Ticket {ticketId}, filed {hour}:{minute}. They have never opened a support ticket in {day}-plus days of storage, and today the first one they file is the one where the answer has to be a number of nines and not a feeling. §1.3: customers never notice you until the day they do.
flavour.ticket.subject.small-upload: uploading our archive! 400 million files, hope that's ok
flavour.ticket.body.small-upload: The enthusiasm is real, the bill is real, the metadata layer is now a question of state. Roughly {smallFileBillions} million objects arrive in one determined weekend and the success you signed up for is reading your index tier like a sponge.
flavour.ticket.subject.invoice-line: what IS this line item on our invoice
flavour.ticket.body.invoice-line: One of their objects got famous. The egress line says {invoiceAmount}, their plan said flat, your rate card said maybe, and all three of you are reading the same sentence with different faces.
flavour.ticket.subject.bucket-question: is {bucketName} supposed to be, and I quote, 'public'
flavour.ticket.body.bucket-question: A security researcher with better manners than your config writer found the listing tonight at {hour}:{minute}. Nothing dramatic happened. Yet. The light is, in fact, spilling.
flavour.abuse.canon.researcher-note: Disclosure: one of your buckets appears to be world-readable. We have not looked inside. Please look inside. — forwarded {ticketId} times before it reached a human with hands.
flavour.abuse.canon.vendor-advisory: Drive firmware advisory: batch {firmwareSerial}. Failure mode: described. Rate: unpriced. Your racks bought this generation together, so the schedule will read like a purchase order.
flavour.press.headline.quiet-death: {hostName} data-loss saga began, auditors say, as a background process nobody scheduled; the redundancy agreed with the bug the whole way down.
flavour.press.headline.dispute: {hostName} customer disputes egress invoice after one asset goes viral; both parties describe the billing model as 'a choice someone made in shift one'.
flavour.forum.thread.nines-promise: Anyone else's marketing says eleven nines while your scrub dashboard says 'finishes in twelve days, good luck'? Because the arithmetic does not care what the landing page promised.
flavour.forum.thread.stacked-shadows: Found three replica shadows stacked on one rack in a demo tenant today and I felt physically ill. Whoever renders durability positionally deserves a medal; whoever placed those three deserves the hole.
flavour.chatter.desk.invisible: Zero tickets about storage this week. On any other line that is a good week. Here it is just next week's cliffhanger.
flavour.chatter.comb.even: The comb looks full and even from altitude. That sentence is either the whole victory or the whole lie, and the meter cannot tell you which.
flavour.codex.scrub: The operational truth that makes durability real: the scrub must complete faster than the failure rate. Not 'fast'. Faster. It is a race with a clock you schedule against, and §1.3 says so out loud.
flavour.codex.no-attacker: There is no dramatic attacker on this line (§1.3 verbatim). The genre is disaster arithmetic: entropy, placement, and rebuilds — the monster is a probability you can compute, and the jump-scare is a spreadsheet.
flavour.loading.tip.show-work: Durability is arithmetic, not vibes. Show your work: replicas, placement, and a scrub that finishes before the next failure is due.
flavour.loading.tip.price-exit: Egress is the revenue line and the landmine in the same column. A customer whose success ruins you was a pricing decision, made in a calm shift, with no incident open.
flavour.intern.entry.firstticket: Day {day}: first support ticket in months and it is not a complaint, it is a question — 'where is my data, exactly?' The boss made me compute the answer. The answer was a dial position.
flavour.intern.entry.shadows: Day {day}: learned the nines by stacking pebbles. Three shadows on one rack look wrong before they ARE wrong, which the senior tech says is the entire level in one drawing.
flavour.sticky.note.placement: Audited placement BEFORE the demo, not after the hole. — postmortem wall, {bucketName} incident
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.canary.comb-tally: {verifiedPct} of the comb verified with {scrubDaysLeft} of cycle left while {egressTB} of egress moved out the door — the scrub clock and the rate card are the same instrument, read twice.
